symptom: PC in VLAN 10 cannot communicate with devices in same VLAN
topology_note: PC1 connected to SW1 Fa0/1; PC2 is in VLAN 10; Fa0/1 should be an access port in VLAN 10
show_output: show vlan brief: Fa0/1 is listed under VLAN 1; VLAN 10 exists and is active
expected_fix: Assign Fa0/1 to VLAN 10 and verify connectivity
evidence_expected: Fa0/1 is shown under VLAN 1 while it should be in VLAN 10.

symptom: PC cannot reach default gateway
show_output: ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.10.20; Default Gateway 192.168.1.1
alternative_faults: ARP failure or gateway interface down
expected_fix: Configure default gateway as 192.168.10.1
evidence_expected: The host is in 192.168.10.0/24 but its configured gateway is in 192.168.1.0/24.

symptom: PC receives no IP address
topology_note: PC is connected to DHCP-enabled VLAN; DHCP server is on the same network
show_output: ipconfig: 169.254.10.5; show ip dhcp pool: 254/254 addresses leased
alternative_faults: Wrong VLAN or DHCP service unavailable
expected_fix: Expand/reconfigure the DHCP pool and renew the client lease
evidence_expected: The DHCP pool shows all 254 addresses leased, so no address is available.

symptom: PC can ping server IP but cannot open server by name
topology_note: DNS server should resolve server.local to 192.168.30.10
show_output: nslookup server.local: request timed out; ping 192.168.30.10 succeeds
alternative_faults: DNS server unreachable; DNS service unavailable
expected_fix: Configure/reach the correct DNS server and verify resolution
evidence_expected: The hostname lookup times out while direct IP connectivity succeeds.

symptom: VLAN 20 users cannot reach VLAN 30 server
topology_note: Router-on-a-stick topology between SW1 and R1; VLAN 30 must cross SW1-R1 trunk
show_output: show interfaces trunk: allowed VLANs 10,20; VLAN 30 absent
expected_fix: Allow VLAN 30 on the trunk and verify the VLAN exists
evidence_expected: VLAN 30 is absent from the trunk allowed list.

symptom: Two different networks cannot communicate
show_output: show ip route: connected 192.168.10.0/24; no route for 192.168.20.0/24
expected_fix: Configure a route to 192.168.20.0/24 via the correct next hop
evidence_expected: The destination 192.168.20.0/24 is absent from the routing table.

symptom: HTTP traffic to server is blocked but ping works
topology_note: ACL is configured on the router interface toward server 10.0.0.10
show_output: show access-lists: deny tcp any host 10.0.0.10 eq 80; ICMP is permitted
expected_fix: Modify the ACL to permit required HTTP traffic
evidence_expected: The ACL explicitly denies TCP port 80 to 10.0.0.10 while ICMP is permitted.

symptom: Internal PC cannot access internet
topology_note: Private LAN uses NAT overload on edge router
show_output: show ip nat translations: empty; show run interface g0/0: no ip nat inside; G0/1 has ip nat outside
expected_fault: NAT not configured on inside interface
expected_fix: Mark the LAN interface as ip nat inside and verify PAT configuration
evidence_expected: The LAN interface lacks ip nat inside and the NAT translation table is empty.

symptom: Wireless client connects to SSID but gets no IP
topology_note: AP is connected to a DHCP-enabled LAN
show_output: ipconfig: 169.254.x.x; show ip dhcp pool: 254/254 addresses leased
expected_fix: Provide available DHCP addresses and renew the wireless client lease
evidence_expected: The client has a link-local address and the DHCP pool has no available addresses.

symptom: Wireless client cannot join Wi-Fi
topology_note: SSID is visible and WPA2 is enabled
show_output: AP security configuration: WPA2-PSK key = NetSage123; client authentication failed with different key
expected_fix: Correct the client/AP security key and reconnect
evidence_expected: The AP and client use different WPA2-PSK keys.

symptom: Interface between router and switch is down
topology_note: R1 G0/0 connects to SW1 G0/1
show_output: show ip interface brief: G0/0 administratively down, line protocol down
expected_fix: Enter no shutdown on G0/0 and verify link status
evidence_expected: G0/0 is administratively down.

symptom: PC intermittently loses network connection
topology_note: PC connected to SW1 Fa0/1 using a damaged cable
show_output: show interfaces fa0/1: input errors 125; CRC 98; line protocol up
expected_fix: Replace the cable/repair the physical connection and retest
evidence_expected: CRC and input errors are increasing on the physical interface.

symptom: Hosts in VLAN 40 cannot communicate though ports are assigned correctly
topology_note: SW1 should have VLAN 40 created
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN 40 is not present; Fa0/5 and Fa0/6 are assigned to default VLAN 1
expected_fix: Create VLAN 40 and assign the required access ports
evidence_expected: VLAN 40 is absent from the switch VLAN database.

symptom: PC gets IP address but wrong subnet mask
topology_note: DHCP pool is intended for a /24 network
expected_fix: Correct the DHCP pool network/mask and renew the client lease
evidence_expected: The client receives /16 instead of the expected /24 mask.

symptom: Branch LAN cannot reach headquarters
topology_note: R1 and R2 are connected by a WAN link; HQ network is 10.10.0.0/24
show_output: show ip route: 10.10.0.0/24 via 172.16.1.9; actual R2 next hop is 172.16.1.2
alternative_faults: WAN link down; incorrect next hop; missing route
next_command: show ip route and show ip interface brief
expected_fix: Correct the static route next-hop address
evidence_expected: The route points to 172.16.1.9 although the actual next hop is 172.16.1.2.

symptom: Only one department cannot access a server
topology_note: Department subnet 192.168.60.0/24 has an ACL on the router
show_output: show access-lists: deny ip 192.168.60.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.20; other departments are permitted
expected_fix: Remove or modify the incorrect ACL deny rule
evidence_expected: The ACL explicitly denies the entire 192.168.60.0/24 subnet to the server.

symptom: Internal hosts access internet but cannot receive return traffic
topology_note: PAT is configured on edge router; G0/0 is inside and G0/1 is outside
show_output: show run interface g0/0: ip nat inside; show run interface g0/1: no ip nat outside
expected_fix: Configure ip nat outside on the Internet-facing interface
evidence_expected: The outside interface has no ip nat outside configuration.

symptom: Two PCs have the same IP and connectivity is unstable
topology_note: PC1 and PC2 are manually configured on the same subnet
show_output: arp -a: 192.168.70.20 appears with different MAC addresses at different times
expected_fix: Assign unique IP addresses and clear stale ARP entries if needed
evidence_expected: The same IP appears with different MAC addresses in ARP.

symptom: PC cannot communicate outside local network
topology_note: PC address is 192.168.70.20/24
show_output: ipconfig: IPv4 192.168.70.20; Default Gateway: blank
expected_fix: Configure the correct default gateway
evidence_expected: The host has no default gateway configured.

symptom: Users cannot browse a website by hostname after DNS server change
topology_note: Clients should use internal DNS 10.0.0.53
show_output: ipconfig /all: DNS Servers 8.8.8.8 only; nslookup internal.example.local: NXDOMAIN
expected_fix: Configure 10.0.0.53 as DNS and verify the internal record
evidence_expected: Clients use 8.8.8.8 instead of internal DNS 10.0.0.53 and the internal name returns NXDOMAIN.

symptom: Inter-VLAN communication fails on router-on-a-stick
topology_note: R1 G0/0 uses subinterfaces for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20
show_output: show run interface g0/0.20: encapsulation dot1Q 200; expected VLAN ID is 20
expected_fix: Change encapsulation to dot1Q 20 and verify trunk VLAN 20
evidence_expected: Subinterface G0/0.20 uses dot1Q 200 instead of VLAN 20.

symptom: Trunk between switches reports native VLAN mismatch
topology_note: SW1 and SW2 are connected by an 802.1Q trunk
show_output: show interfaces trunk: SW1 native VLAN 99; SW2 native VLAN 1; native VLAN mismatch warning
expected_fix: Configure the same native VLAN on both trunk endpoints
evidence_expected: The two trunk endpoints use different native VLANs: 99 and 1.

symptom: DHCP clients receive addresses but cannot reach gateway
topology_note: DHCP server distributes options for subnet 192.168.80.0/24
show_output: show running-config | section dhcp: default-router 192.168.80.254; actual gateway is 192.168.80.1
expected_fix: Change DHCP default-router to 192.168.80.1 and renew leases
evidence_expected: The DHCP pool advertises 192.168.80.254 while the actual gateway is 192.168.80.1.

symptom: Remote network unreachable after adding a new subnet
topology_note: Three routers are connected in a chain; new subnet 192.168.100.0/24 is behind R3
show_output: show ip route ospf: no 192.168.100.0/24; show run | section router ospf: R3 network statement does not include 192.168.100.0/24
alternative_faults: OSPF advertisement missing; static route missing; OSPF adjacency problem
next_command: show ip ospf neighbor and show ip protocols
expected_fix: Add the new network to OSPF and verify route propagation
evidence_expected: OSPF does not advertise the new 192.168.100.0/24 network.

symptom: Guest Wi-Fi can access internal company server
topology_note: Guest SSID should be isolated from internal VLAN 10
show_output: show access-lists: no deny rule from guest VLAN 50 to 192.168.10.0/24; permit rule allows traffic
alternative_faults: Guest SSID mapped to wrong VLAN
expected_fix: Add an ACL denying guest-to-internal traffic while allowing Internet access
evidence_expected: The ACL has no deny rule protecting the internal subnet from guest VLAN 50.

symptom: External users cannot reach published internal web server
topology_note: Static NAT should map public 203.0.113.10 to server 192.168.90.10
show_output: show ip nat translations: no static mapping for 192.168.90.10; running-config has no static NAT entry
expected_fix: Configure the required static NAT mapping and verify outside connectivity
evidence_expected: No static NAT entry exists for 192.168.90.10.

symptom: PC connected to switch cannot reach any device
topology_note: Access port should operate at 100 Mbps full duplex
show_output: show interfaces fa0/5: line protocol down; speed 10Mb/s, duplex half; switch port expected 100Mb/s full
alternative_faults: Duplex mismatch; damaged cable; interface shutdown
expected_fix: Correct speed/duplex settings or use auto-negotiation and verify link
evidence_expected: The interface reports half duplex/10 Mbps while the expected configuration is 100 Mbps full duplex.

symptom: Network devices cannot reach DNS server after ACL update
topology_note: Router filters traffic to DNS server 10.10.10.53
show_output: show access-lists: deny udp any host 10.10.10.53 eq 53; DNS queries time out; ping to DNS server succeeds
expected_fix: Permit required DNS UDP/53 traffic in the ACL
evidence_expected: The ACL explicitly denies UDP/53 to the DNS server.

symptom: Wireless users experience poor connectivity in one area
topology_note: Two nearby APs use overlapping 2.4 GHz channels
show_output: AP status: AP1 channel 6, AP2 channel 6; high channel utilization and interference reported
expected_fix: Assign non-overlapping channels and verify interference decreases
evidence_expected: Both APs use channel 6 and channel utilization/interference is high.

symptom: PC in correct VLAN cannot reach gateway after switch replacement
topology_note: Gateway is connected through a trunk to the distribution switch; VLAN 50 is required
show_output: show interfaces trunk: trunk operational; allowed VLANs 10,20,30; VLAN 50 absent
expected_fault: Required VLAN missing from trunk allowed list
expected_fix: Add VLAN 50 to the trunk allowed list and verify gateway reachability
evidence_expected: VLAN 50 is absent from the trunk allowed list.
